notes.text:
Retain K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), t=s^8 and X=(G_m^2)^an/<(t,2),(3,t)>. My independent scoped mathematical decision is positive for whole383's finite Picard/nonalgebraization and ordinary bounded/operator/energy/circle chain under its explicitly checked published analytic foundations. No incoming correctness grant is used. This is an unverified research draft; original closure is false.

Finite Picard proof. Gruson, Fibres vectoriels sur un polydisque ultrametrique (1968), IV.5 Theorem 1, gives SK^0(H)=coker(Z->K^0(H))=0 for finite completed products of his disc and unit-circle algebras over a complete real-valued field. Wide annuli are not inputs to this theorem. A rank-one projective P has [P]=[H], hence P+Q is isomorphic to H+Q; determinants cancel det Q and give P=H. Induct on the number of wide factors: for A(r,R) times Y, its restriction to C(r) times Y is trivial by induction. Glue to a trivial bundle on D(r) times Y. Inside D(R) times Y these are a finite rational G-cover, with inequalities |z/a|<=1 and |a/z|<=1, |a|=r; a is a constant unit, (a,z) is the unit ideal, and the intersection is exactly C(r) times Y. Coherent invertible-sheaf descent and induction trivialize the filled bundle and therefore the original bundle. Thus every finite product, and every nested polyannulus P_m over this K, has Picard group zero. Van der Put, Rigid analytic spaces, GAU J7, 2.14--2.16.3 supplies coherent affinoid correspondence/descent; its completed-tensor argument and actual PDF page 10, printed J7-09, were examined, with the necessary cocycle and its deeper Kiehl attribution explicit.

On nested P_m, normalize successive frames by scalar monomials. Unit Gauss estimates make the remaining factors 1+g_m satisfy ||g_m||_(P_j)<=|s|^(m-j) for m>j. Convergent products give compatible global frames, so Pic((G_m^2)^an)=0; global units are scalar monomials. Commuting the periods forces multiplier exponents h_1=(0,k), h_2=(k,0). For k!=0 choose n=(1,sign k): v(lambda(n)^h)=2|k|>0, and Laurent coefficient recurrence has quadratic negative leading valuation, contradicting convergence. For k=0 every nonzero section is a single monomial. Every intrinsic meromorphic pole ideal is coherent invertible by regular local UFD cancellation and flat restriction. A global frame supplies two analytic sections with the same multipliers; their ratio is constant. Thus Gamma(X,M)=K.

The action relation is closed and locally finite. Quotient charts and a compact polyannulus fundamental domain make X good, strict, smooth, connected, separated, proper, boundaryless and two-dimensional. A hypothetical separated finite-type K-algebraic space Y with Y^an=X is smooth connected integral of dimension two. Conrad--Temkin 2.3.1--2.3.2 and 4.2.3--4.2.4 supply checked reflection/gluing/coherent descent; Ducros 2.1.4 supplies regular, hence flat, algebraic-to-analytic local maps. With every generic-field hypothesis checked, Stacks 0ENA/0END/0EN6/0BB1/086U identify K(Y), and coherent analytification injects it into Gamma(X,M)=K, contradicting trdeg_K K(Y)=2. This excludes all such algebraic spaces over base K; arbitrary extensions are not claimed.

The datum theta=DD(|x|^2/2), x_j=-log|z_j|, has genuine raw mass two. C_theta consists of continuous weights locally uniformly approximable on ordinary opens by smooth middle-positive weights. PSD order-unit domination on Sym(Lambda^p), coefficient Radon measures and continuous multiplication yield genuine bounded symmetric/local/uniformly continuous products. Smooth closed-factor Leibniz is used; arbitrary continuous closedness is not. Canonical analytic degree-one calibration gives theta^2=2i_*dx. Stokes gives mass two and bounded comparison. The complete branch-energy, circle Green-function, separable Hessian/measure/energy, obstacle-chord orthogonality and circle first-variation arguments are reproduced in the standalone paper; they do not recognize all psh or all analytic obstacles.

notes.summary: New genuine identity MA(U_N)=delta_o+delta_xi_N and explicit bounded solutions for finite nested branch measures of total branch mass at most one.
notes.detailedSummary: A refined ordinary moment argument identifies the previously unspecified mass at the original Gauss point. Successive squared coefficient tails give every branch atom and permit square-root inversion. These are genuine bounded products on the nonalgebraizable analytic space, with uniqueness only inside the stated finite family and no universal branch cap or full-class admissibility claim.
notes.text:
Use n1's actual analytic X, datum theta and bounded calculus. Put G(a)=a^2/2-a/2+1/12 periodically on R/Z, u0=-G(x_1)-G(x_2), o=i(0), y=(1,1). On the ordinary sheet about x=0 set w_j=z_j-1 and W={|w_1|<1,|w_2|<1}. Define R=-log max(|w_1|,|w_2|) on W, zero outside, and D_N=-min(N,R), U_N=u0+D_N. The ordinary refined-chart proof applies to every real N>0: inactive zero coordinates are omitted. Let xi_N be the translated Gauss point of w-radii exp(-N).

New identity: MA(U_N)=delta_o+delta_xi_N. The established branch computation gives mass one at xi_N and support in F=tau^(-1)(0). On F with exactly one |w_j|<1 the local weight is affine in unit logarithms, so top mass vanishes. Where all |z_j|=|w_j|=1, use the common moment (z_1,w_1,z_2,w_2). CLD-v2 8.8.6 supports the bounded tropical product on its top moment skeleton; 12.2.7--10 bounds local tropical dimension by the transcendence degree of the graded reductions of these coordinates. Dependent reductions z_1,z_2 give dimension at most one. Independent reductions force every Laurent polynomial to have its original unit Gauss norm, hence the unique point o. The only remaining mass is therefore at o; total mass two proves the identity. Full applied statements/immediate arguments, including the deeper local-dimension citation, are retained in the source ledger.

For 0<N_1<...<N_k, c_i>=0 and C=sum c_i<=1, set u=u0+sum c_iD_(N_i), C_i=sum_(j>=i)c_j, C_(k+1)=0. Then MA(u)=(2-C^2)delta_o+sum_i p_i delta_xi_(N_i), p_i=C_i^2-C_(i+1)^2. Locally at xi_(N_i), the weight is b max(v_1,v_2)+c max(0,v_1,v_2), b=C_(i+1), c=c_i. Its gradient polygon has area ((b+c)^2-b^2)/2. The softmax Hessian is a positive covariance, its gradient maps diffeomorphically onto the polygon interior, and change of variables gives that area. Actual translated degree one and exterior factor two give p_i. Between depths the square vanishes. Outside W the same refined moment support proof leaves only o. This computes genuine analytic products, rather than defining an inverse measure.

Every finite target (2-P)delta_o+sum p_i delta_xi_(N_i), p_i>=0, P=sum p_i<=1, is solved by c_i=sqrt(sum_(j>=i)p_j)-sqrt(sum_(j>i)p_j). The masses recover every coefficient, giving uniqueness modulo constants within this family. Its energy is E(u)=-1/6-S/3, S=sum_i p_i sum_j c_j min(N_i,N_j). The three energy integrals are 0,-1/6,-1/3-S because the D_N annihilate the theta and alpha_u0 coefficient measures. No bound of one for arbitrary potentials, full measure criterion, or full-domain uniqueness follows.

notes.summary: The actual finite-depth mass-two Dirac has exact restricted dual 1/6+5N0/3; its full intrinsic admissibility remains unresolved.
notes.detailedSummary: The dual is optimized over every finite nonnegative branch mixture with total coefficient at most one. Its maximizer has genuine measure delta_o+delta_xi_N0, rather than the prescribed mass-two Dirac. Restricted finiteness is neither a full-class admissibility proof nor a universal obstruction.
notes.text:
Let B contain every finite mixture from n2, with arbitrary positive real depths and additive constants. Fix the actual analytic point xi_(N0), 0<N0<infinity; it is not the rigid y. For T(t)=sum_(N_i>=t)c_i, 0<=T<=1, n2 and Tonelli give S=integral T^3 and -sum c_iD_(N_i)(xi_(N0))=integral_0^N0 T. Thus E(u)-2u(xi_(N0))=1/6+integral_0^N0(2T-T^3/3)-(1/3)integral_N0^infinity T^3. The first integrand is increasing on [0,1] with maximum 5/3; the second term is nonpositive. T=1 on (0,N0), zero after, attains the upper bound. Consequently sup_B(E(u)-2u(xi_(N0)))=1/6+5N0/3, attained by U_(N0).

More generally the B-dual of mu_p=(2-p)delta_o+p delta_xi_(N0), 0<=p<=2, is 1/6+N0 times (2p^(3/2)/3 for p<=1; p-1/3 for p>=1), by maximizing pT-T^3/3. For p<=1 the maximizer u0+sqrt(p)D_(N0) genuinely solves the equation. For p>1 the maximizer is U_(N0), whose MA is delta_o+delta_xi_(N0), not mu_p.

This universal restricted calculation supplies only a lower bound for the full C_theta dual. It does not prove full admissibility of 2delta_xi_(N0), nonexistence of an arbitrary all-direction solution, or a universal atom cap. The infinite-dual rigid-point test does not apply at fixed finite depth. Complete proof: notes/n3.md and proof-companion.md; rerun python audit_and_build.py for the finite diagnostic identities.

notes.summary: New restricted intrinsic unbounded radial energy theory: genuine full-mass mixed products, comparison, separated compactness, first variation and countable branch equations.
notes.detailedSummary: On a fixed discrete depth grid tending to infinity, summable nonnegative coefficients of total at most one define locally bounded potentials off one rigid point. Genuine local bounded products and verified nonpluripolar truncations give mass two. Finite energy is exactly integrability of the cubic coefficient tail. Normalized energy-bounded subsets are compact in a separated local-uniform topology off the point, with decreasing continuity and all segment variations inside this domain. Square-root tails solve its countable branch range uniquely modulo constants. This is a complete scoped construction, not the full all-direction class or full measure criterion.
notes.text:
Fix 0<N_1<N_2<... tending to infinity. With n2's R and u0, define Gamma by u=u0-H(R)+b, b in R, H(r)=integral_0^r T(t)dt, T(t)=sum_(N_i>=t)c_i, c_i>=0, C=sum c_i<=1. Use the canonical limiting value at y, possibly minus infinity. Partial finite sums decrease to u locally uniformly off y, since R is bounded on compact subsets there and the coefficient tails vanish. Thus genuine bounded local products already exist on X minus {y}. No operator is assigned solely to an unsupported global limit.

For C_i=sum_(j>=i)c_j, local uniform continuity and n2 give MA(u)=(2-C^2)delta_o+sum_i(C_i^2-C_(i+1)^2)delta_xi_(N_i), extended by zero at y. The telescoping tail tends to zero, so this positive analytic Radon measure has full raw mass two. If H(infinity)<infinity, partial sums converge uniformly globally and it agrees with the bounded operator. Otherwise the singular locus is exactly {y}. Truncations u^(M)=u0+b-min(H(R),M) belong to C_theta: if H(infinity)<=M this is the bounded u; otherwise clipped finite sums converge uniformly locally off y and are eventually constant relative to u0 near y. Convex max regularization in the same ordinary charts gives the required approximants. On {H<M}, bounded locality gives the constructed product; the extra clamp atom is excluded. Omitted mass is bounded by T(r)^2 at depth r and tends to zero. This verifies the genuine full-mass nonpluripolar truncation recipe. For large j, max(u,-j) has the same clamp with M=j+b-1/6, since u0=-1/6 on W.

For two such potentials, polarization locally off y gives the genuine mixed product B(u,v)=(2-C_u C_v)delta_o+sum_i(C_i^u C_i^v-C_(i+1)^u C_(i+1)^v)delta_xi_(N_i). Its coefficients are nonnegative, telescope, and give mass two with zero rigid atom; mixed truncations verify full mass. Positivity, symmetry and locality follow from the existing bounded products.

Tonelli computes sum_i(C_i^2-C_(i+1)^2)H(N_i)=integral T^3. The three energy integrals for b=0 are 0,-1/6,-1/3-integral T^3. Therefore Gamma^1 is exactly the domain integral T^3<infinity, with E(u)=-1/6-(1/3)integral T^3+2b. Canonical finite-sum energies decrease to this value. An explicit genuinely unbounded example is N_i=i, c_i=1/(i(i+1)): C_i=1/i, H(infinity)=sum 1/(i+1)=infinity but integral T^3=sum 1/i^3<infinity. Its MA is delta_o+sum_i(1/i^2-1/(i+1)^2)delta_xi_i, with no rigid atom.

For a segment, T_t=(1-t)T+tS, Holder justifies E'=-integral(S-T)T_t^2+2b' and signed Fubini identifies this with integral(v-u)MA(u_t). No undefined difference at y is integrated because its mass is zero. E''=-2integral(S-T)^2T_t<=0, so energy is concave and monotone under pointwise order in this domain. Comparison also holds within Gamma: canonical finite sums have total-variation convergent atomic measures and locally uniformly convergent potentials off y. Choose epsilon avoiding the countable potential differences at o and xi_(N_i); indicators stabilize at each fixed atom, while uniformly small branch tails control the rest. Pass bounded comparison to MA(v){u<v-epsilon}<=MA(u){u<=v-epsilon}, then let epsilon decrease to zero. This compares only Gamma potentials.

All b=0 potentials have supremum 1/12. After normalization, integral T^3<=L implies rT(r)^3<=L, hence coefficient tail <=(L/r)^(1/3) and mass tail <=(L/r)^(2/3). Coordinatewise subsequences of the c_i have no loss of total coefficient; H converges uniformly on finite intervals, and Fatou preserves the energy bound. The parameter set is a closed subset of compact metrizable [0,1]^N, and the tail estimate gives compactness in the local-uniform topology off y. This topology is separated: H recovers every coefficient and the canonical value at y, while normalization fixes b. Actual MA measures converge weakly. For decreasing normalized sequences with the same energy bound, H_m increases, its grid slopes converge, and these estimates identify the limit in Gamma^1. Local uniform and measure continuity follow; energy monotonicity and Fatou give convergence of energies.

For target mu=(2-P)delta_o+sum_i p_i delta_xi_(N_i), p_i>=0, P=sum p_i<=1 and no rigid atom, put P_i=sum_(j>=i)p_j and c_i=sqrt(P_i)-sqrt(P_(i+1)). The genuine operator equals mu, has finite energy exactly when integral P_tail^(3/2)<infinity, and recovers every coefficient, so uniqueness modulo constants holds within Gamma^1. Its dual over all Gamma^1 is 1/6+(2/3)integral P_tail^(3/2): the objective is 1/6+integral(P_tail T-T^3/3), optimized by T=sqrt(P_tail). Finite optimizing coefficient cutoffs and monotone convergence establish divergence if the integral is infinite. This criterion is restricted to the stated range and is not full intrinsic admissibility. If the grid includes N0, 2delta_xi_(N0) still has the finite restricted value in n3, while no Gamma solution has branch mass two. This is not an original counterexample.
